verdict.rationale: Nix's own docs show that system and fleet configurations are declared in Nix expression files, built atomically, and can be rolled back to earlier states. That covers the versioning and rollback parts of the story for declarative automation. Nothing documents a review step such as diffing or approving changes, and 'automations' is only approximated by declarative system and service configuration. missing for 10: a documented review/diff workflow for configuration changes, explicit versioning or history browsing of automations, independent hands-on corroboration of rollback.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: By building entire system configurations from a Nix expression, NixOS ensures that such configurations don’t overwrite each other, can be rolled back, and so on.
Describe a laptop or a fleet of servers in reversable and repeatable configuration.
it is easy to roll back the entire configuration of the system to an earlier state

you can roll back to the old version:
$ nix-env --rollback
